reading.body:
Tome is recorded here as a single product, an AI presentation and storytelling tool, with one MCP integration for customer data analysis.

The data covers a company entry and nothing more. There is no funding, headcount, revenue, model provider, or infrastructure detail, so nothing here speaks to compute, buildings, or power. The one integration listed, ai.saifs/customer-intelligence, points at sales segmentation rather than at the presentation product itself, which suggests the tool is being wired into a customer workflow rather than used only for slide generation.

What the entry does not tell the reader is scale. A single product and a single integration are consistent with an early company and with a narrow public listing, and this data cannot distinguish between them. It also gives no date for when the product or integration appeared, only the date the record was built.

For AI specifically, the useful signal is category. Presentation generation sits in the application layer, where value comes from interface and output quality rather than from owned compute. That layer is the least exposed to the grid constraint and the most exposed to whatever model access it rents. Nothing in this record shows which models Tome uses or where they run.

The integration listed is not for the presentation product. It is a customer intelligence tool that segments customers and predicts which ones to focus on for sales. That means Tome's public record includes a sales-facing capability alongside its storytelling product, and the two do not obviously share a surface. A reader looking for the company's AI story finds instead a company whose listed AI work is about customer data, not slides.

The record is a single product and a single integration with no dates attached to either. The only timestamp is the build date of the record itself, 2026-10-03. That makes the entry consistent with a company that has one product and one integration, and equally consistent with a company whose other products and integrations are simply not listed here. The data cannot separate a small company from a partially documented one.

For the compute thesis, the category is the whole signal. Presentation generation is an application-layer product. It rents model access rather than owning compute, so it carries no building, no power contract, and no grid exposure of its own. Whatever constraint applies to Tome applies through its model provider, and this record names no provider.

What is Tome's product?
Tome is listed as a single product in the Slides and Presentations category, described as AI storytelling, presentation generation, narrative design, and creative IP.

What is the MCP integration for?
It is ai.saifs/customer-intelligence, which analyzes customer data for segmentation and predicts which customers to focus on for more sales.

Does the data say which AI models Tome uses?
No. The record contains no model provider, no infrastructure detail, and no compute information of any kind.

Does the data show Tome's funding, headcount, or revenue?
No. None of those fields appear in the record.

When did Tome's product or integration launch?
The data does not hold a launch date for either. The only date present is the record's build date, 2026-10-03.

Is Tome exposed to the grid constraint on AI scaling?
Not directly through anything in this record. As an application-layer presentation tool it would rent model access, and the record names no owned compute, buildings, or power.
